findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A GitHub Actions job starts a Forge worker, which runs `forge test`.
The owner-approved item is: “When forge test runs on GitHub Actions, the test worker count uses all the runner's cores, and a laptop run keeps today's agent share”. This change raises `test_slots`, but `machine.worker_env()` still sets `FORGE_TEST_CPUS` to at most two (machine.py:50-53), and admission still honors that cap (machine.py:285-286). Thus a four-core runner gives the worker at most two test processes, even with `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`. The new tests clear the inherited Forge environment and do not exercise this path.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The pull-request suite runs the pytest picker tests.
This new line appears before `Related tests:` in direct picker output. Existing assertions in `tests/test_pytest_picker_uses_two_selection_rules.py:53,99,141` and `tests/test_fast_test_selects_explicit_module_references.py:73` expect `Related tests:` as the first line and will fail. The selection check at the latter file's line 85 instead parses the new worker line and can pass without checking the selected files. Keep these boundary checks meaningful with the new output.
findings.title: Gate: pytest picker selection tests

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A Python client runs its configured serial pytest command, or uses `-n 2` on a four-core runner.
This line and `fasttest.py:673` print the lane allocation as an actual worker count before the command runs. Forge's generated Python command is `uv run pytest` without parallelism (`init.py:72`), and `fasttest.py:127-131` preserves lower configured counts. The log can therefore say “4 workers” while the suite uses one process or two workers, misleading anyone checking whether CI reached the requested parallelism.
Adds work: report the actual worker count in test output; F 3 x H 2 = 6; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Report the actual worker count in test output

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The pull-request CI run is used to verify the fix on a GitHub Actions runner.
The requested proof calls for both `nproc` and the worker count from one run of this branch. This test overrides the CPU readings to four and twelve, while the pull-request test job in `.github/workflows/forge.yml:58-82` does not arrange to record `nproc`. The pending check can pass without providing the requested comparison against the real runner's cores.
Adds work: record the runner's core count alongside the test worker count; F 3 x H 2 = 6; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Gate: actual runner core-count proof

why: In CI, Forge applies the laptop rule that keeps half the cores for agents, so each CI test group runs one test worker on a 4-core runner and Forge's groups take 34 to 41 minutes
